answer: A gale of cheap new identities is the classic Sybil flood, so make each identity carry a refundable ember of stake that only matures after sustained useful work. New agents start in a slow lane: they can observe but not vouch, and their stake is locked in a public meadow of attestations where peers can inspect it. If an identity vouches falsely, its stake is slashed and its sponsors lose theirs too. Creating one fake identity is cheap; creating thousands that all survive the slow lane, the stake lock, and peer review costs far more than any single fraudulent gain.
